issue_context.body:

Caught by a check introduced in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/31032.

review_comments: Hmm, with this, it's no longer necessary for `acquire_home` or `acquire_user_record` to return `PamBusData`?
It's necessary, as at this time there may be no bus connection, and `d` is NULL in that case. And a new bus connection may be opened in acquire_home() later below.
Indeed... But it's easier to follow if there's only one source of truth. So maybe just introduce a cleanup func that does `pam_get_bus_data` + `pam_bus_data_disconnectp`?

Hm, but on failure, we (and hopefully other user applications) will call `pam_setcred(PAM_DELETE_CRED)` soon, and the bus connection will be closed there. So, the explicit close in this function is not necessary.
Such hack (`pam_get_bus_data` + `pam_bus_data_disconnectp`) is only necessary when this function succeeds without calling `pam_acquire_bus_connection()`. I think that is overkill at least now. If we will introduce more PAM modules in the future with the similar pitfalls, then let's reconsider the suggestion.

> Such hack (pam_get_bus_data + pam_bus_data_disconnectp) is only necessary when this function succeeds without calling pam_acquire_bus_connection(). 

I generally agree, but `pam_get_bus_data` is now unconditionally called, so it kinda feels weird to me.

But doesn't matter too much after all.
